verdict: Broadcom grew revenue 25% to a record $14.9B as AI chip sales jumped 77% and VMware lifted software revenue 47%, and net income more than quadrupled to $5.5B as the heavy one-off costs of the VMware deal faded.

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. AI semiconductor revenue grew 77% YoY to $4.1B.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — the steady, subscription side of the company, up 47% YoY with a full quarter of VMware included.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next chips and software — a smaller share of each revenue dollar than most chip rivals spend.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization & restructuring
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in acquisitions (VMware above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — plus restructuring and other charges.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $873M on Broadcom's debt, partly offset by $103M of other income — a net -$770M below operating profit.
footerNote: The tax line was a small benefit, not a bill: a $13M income-tax benefit is drawn as a green source into net profit.

takeaways.title: AI chips are the growth engine
takeaways.text: AI semiconductor revenue grew 77% YoY to $4.1B, and Broadcom guided it to $4.4B in the next quarter as hyperscale customers kept investing in custom AI chips and data-center networking.

takeaways.title: VMware is the steady half
takeaways.text: Infrastructure software revenue rose 47% to $6.7B — 45% of all revenue — giving Broadcom a subscription base that smooths the ups and downs of chip sales.

takeaways.title: A cash machine
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $6.0B — 40% of revenue — even while carrying the debt taken on to buy VMware; interest on that debt cost $873M in the quarter.

oneTimers: GAAP profit carries $1,995M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets ($1,484M inside cost of revenue and $511M inside operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $7,823M instead of $5,503M.
